author: harness:codex

patch.value: Enforce docstring and erasable-TypeScript quality gates in the starter reference

The canonical reference still lacks fail-closed gates for 100% docstring coverage, explicit unsafe TypeScript syntax, duplication, and its legacy merge-driver preparation helper remains JavaScript. The 2026.8.7 compatibility pass removed all explicit any annotations and dynamic imports from TypeScript tests, but a reusable audited gate is required so copied packages cannot regress.

a tested TypeScript quality gate covers every repository-owned TypeScript source and fails on missing docstrings explicit any dynamic imports and non-erasable syntax; the merge-driver preparation helper is TypeScript with exact behavioral coverage and no JavaScript replacement; duplication thresholds and exclusions are explicit tested and required in CI and release:check; npm and Bun paths pass exact 100/100/100 coverage and the new quality gates

CI and release:check enforce 100% high-quality docstrings for executable TypeScript, reject explicit any and non-erasable or dynamic-import syntax, run duplication analysis with justified exclusions, and use TypeScript for repository-owned executable helpers.
Exact runtime coverage is enforced, but those source-quality properties are review-only and scripts/prepare-merge-driver.mjs remains a repository-owned JavaScript helper.
Agents copy this repository as the extension baseline, so unenforced quality debt propagates to every derived package.

message: Track fail-closed starter source-quality gates discovered during the 2026.8.7 compatibility audit
